title: to_char(timestamptz,'TZ') heap overflow write, ~36 B -- stays inside its aset block
live_proof: CVE-2026-14669, fixed upstream in 12a6206864a0, which postdates the 17.5 pin. Reproduced on the pin: PostgreSQL's own MEMORY_CONTEXT_CHECKING reports 'detected write past chunk end' in ExprContext, followed by four alloc-set integrity warnings
fidelity: real server, real allocator, upstream's own trigger shape. The overflow is about 36 bytes and stays inside its aset block, so ASan is structurally blind to it, and so are capability bounds on the block or the arena (cheribsd-revocation, spatial). It does leave its aset chunk: PostgreSQL's own check reports damaged chunk headers (bad chunk size, bad block offset), and the sublet arm, which bounds each aset chunk, faults on the store (cause 7, 2026-10-05) -- that is the measurement, not a weakness of the case

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: completes; the defect is witnessed by PostgreSQL's own check or by the differential -- REACHED-SILENT (2026-10-04, probe run). Plain purecap rc=0, no fault. The cassert build's own MEMORY_CONTEXT_CHECKING fires: detected write past chunk end; bad chunk size; bad block offset; req size > alloc size; found inconsistent memory block. The overflow stays inside the palloc chunk, so CHERI is correct to stay silent -- but the defect provably executed.
cheribsd-revocation.evidence: ran to the prompt with no fault
cheribsd-revocation.run: run 2026-10-06 by the corpus's own runner (shared/run-arm.py for the Capstone arms, shared/run-cheribsd.sh for the purecap one); see results/

virtual-malloc.oracle: virtual profile, PostgreSQL's contexts stock (tools/arms.json virtual-mallocng): a fault after the trigger started that its control.sql or a justified fault_sites ties to the defect, or the trigger completes and this arm did not see it
virtual-malloc.verdict_note: reached (the trigger statement ran (3 prompts, 0 setup line(s))) and completed with no fault

virtual-pg-pools.oracle: virtual profile with the memory-context port's patch 0003: every palloc chunk a child lifetime of its block (CDERIVE), revoked by pfree and repalloc (CREVOKE) (tools/arms.json virtual-mallocng-pg-pools): as virtual-malloc
virtual-pg-pools.verdict_note: cause=28 pc=0x3fa2001a7c in __stpcpy; by function: __stpcpy is a declared fault site

status: measured on virtual Capstone (virtual-malloc, virtual-pg-pools) and stock CheriBSD (cheribsd-revocation); each arm's verdict_from names its bundle. The physical spatial/sublet pair measured 2026-10-06 to 2026-10-10 stays in results/
nested_why: The object is a palloc chunk, which AllocSet carves out of a block it took from malloc, so the defect is nested by the allocator that served it.
fault_sites_why: The overflow is the copy of the time-zone name into the result buffer: DCH_to_char's case DCH_TZ does strcpy(s, tmtcTzn(in)) (src/backend/utils/adt/formatting.c:2900, 17.5) with no bound on s, and musl's strcpy is __stpcpy(dest, src) (src/string/strcpy.c), so the out-of-bounds write lands in __stpcpy. Declared 2026-10-10 after the virtual-pg-pools run resolved its fault there; the reason is the 17.5 source cited, which does not depend on that run.
